title: Self-powered UV sensing with perovskite/polymer nanocomposites
summary: Explored fluorescent CsPbBr3@Cs4PbBr6 perovskite/polymer nanocomposites and translated their response into a self-powered UV-sensing device.
problem: How can a functional material convert an environmental stimulus into a useful signal without depending on a separate power source?
approach: The work connected materials synthesis with structural, optical and device-level characterisation, followed by fabrication and performance analysis.
what_it_shows: This project represents the experimental side of my research identity: working across chemistry, materials and device behaviour rather than treating them as separate stages.
next: A future direction is to make this kind of workflow more predictive by combining experimental understanding with computational screening.

title: Ferroelectric switching and interfacial charge retention
summary: Studying how switching behaviour and interfacial charge retention shape the electrical response of ferroelectric thin-film devices.
problem: What controls the retention and switching behaviour that determine whether a ferroelectric device is simply interesting or genuinely useful?
approach: The work combines thin-film preparation with electrical measurements and analysis of polarisation switching and charge-retention behaviour.
what_it_shows: It adds a device-physics and interface perspective to my materials background, with emphasis on understanding the mechanisms behind measured behaviour.
next: The longer-term aim is to connect experimental measurements with theoretical and computational approaches so that promising device conditions can be identified earlier.
